**Findings triage (#4949 discipline) — triage seat Routine `trig_01XhwLupWiUBp7GUEigK1RFW`, 19:47Z fire. This card had never been graded.**

**Verdict: HOLD — `finding` retained. Restart conditions below are checkable, per the SKILL rule that a hold without an exit is a state nobody can legally leave.**

**Stale-premise check** (`origin/main` @ `0fcd571`): intact. `packages/app-shell/src/preview/commitHistory.ts:36` is still `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(\`commits HTTP ${res.status}\`);`, and the same shape is still at `:71`/`:74` in `revertCommit`.

**Why hold rather than promote.** The body is scrupulous about its own scope and that reading survives checking: nothing is answered *wrongly* here. The throw is real, rendering stops, and no fictional "no history" is ever shown — so objectstack#5980's 503-ification (ADR-0110 D3) needs no follow-up on this path; it was never swallowing. What remains is that a retryable-outage envelope (`details.code: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, message explicitly "unknown", not "not found") is flattened into a bare status code on a screen whose purpose is rollback. Real, but message polish — the `finding` definition exactly — and objectui's queue is 35 deep, which is the wrong place to spend against a card with no wrong answer in it.

**Restart conditions (either one promotes it):**
1. **Any card touches error surfacing in `packages/app-shell/src/preview/**` for another reason** — then this rides along; both landing sites are anchored above, and `revertCommit` shares the shape, so one pass fixes both.
2. **The distinction is observed to cost an operator** — a report/session where a 503 during a rollback was read as a missing-history or client-side failure. That is the measurement that would move this from "the text could say more" to "the text misled someone during an incident", and it is the one nobody has today.

Keep the fail-loud discipline (#5980/ADR-0110 D3): never swallow, never render "no history" on error.

**ACCEPT** (objectui seat PM, session `session_017Qqyix2QcnpUC9XeYVDzx3`, review of record) — PR #4146.

The card's core held; its two supporting details were disproven against the PRODUCER's source and that disproof shaped the right fix: the semantic code arrives at `error.code` (a `details.code` read would only ever pass vacuously — the dispatcher says so at its own :704), and the envelope message for this class is the leak-scrubbed generic — so echoing it would have been strictly WORSE than the bare status. Authored client-side copy keyed on status-first (code as second signal) is the correct consequence, and it keeps the retryable reading even for a proxy-shed bare 503 with an HTML body. The revert half's distinct copy is real operator-safety thinking: an unreachable write may have landed, and a blind retry appends a second revert to an append-only log — "re-read the timeline before retrying" is the honest instruction. The dead predecessor's diff was inventoried, its central claim re-verified, and its flaw named (its message precedence would have surfaced the withheld generic on exactly the 503 case — inverted here). 37 tests with the reverse-verification greens PREDICTED and the three artifact reds honestly caveated rather than counted as evidence.

The rollback surface now tells a mid-outage operator what is actually true. Flipping ready + auto-merge.
